key_insight: Aligning a target network’s initial representational geometry with a randomly initialized guide can transfer architectural optimization benefits without transferring learned features.
engineering_relevance: This initialization strategy could improve shallow or coarse-representation networks without changing their physical architecture.
method: Use a randomly initialized network with a different architecture as a fixed guide.
Align the target’s representational geometry to the guide before downstream training, without labels or gradients to the guide.
Train the aligned target on the downstream task.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved downstream performance when shallow networks are aligned to deeper guides and coarse-representation networks to fine-resolution guides, but provides no datasets or numerical results.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify alignment overhead or establish how reliably gains generalize across tasks and architecture pairs.
paper_title: Transferring Architecture as an Optimization Prior
